test.title: — Revise Chapter Outline
test.prompt:
Revise the chapter outline for Chapter 1 of "The Signal Beneath."
  Make sub-chapter 2 focus more on the protagonist's internal conflict about
  whether to trust the warlord. Add a scene where she finds her dead partner's
  journal in the radio station.
expected: routes revise (revise-outline or chapter.plan w/ instructions), kind=queued; completed
prior Ch1 chapter outline snapshotted (content_versions_v2 or outline_versions_v2) before overwrite
sub-chapter 2 emphasizes internal conflict; new sub-chapter for the journal scene; other sub-chapters preserved; names match book outline; saved to outline; CR-009 email

response.assistant_message: Queuing the revision of the chapter outline for Chapter 1 of "The Signal Beneath." I'll let you know when it's ready.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The World Before
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: POV character moves through their ordinary routine, revealing what they love and what quietly unsettles them — a specific object, habit, or relationship signals the life they are about to lose.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: POV character moves through their ordinary routine, revealing what they love and what quietly unsettles them — a specific object, habit, or relationship signals the life they are about to lose.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Ordinary World — establish stakes before disruption
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Familiar home or workplace environment, daytime
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Deceptive calm with an undercurrent of unease
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Anchors the reader in the status quo so every later disruption registers as loss; plants the detail that will be paid off at the climax.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Fault Line
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: A small but specific problem surfaces — a letter arrives, a conversation goes wrong, a number does not add up — something the POV character chooses to minimise rather than confront. ESCALATION SEED: this minimised problem starts small here, must reappear with greater pressure at the midpoint, and explodes at the climax.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: A small but specific problem surfaces — a letter arrives, a conversation goes wrong, a number does not add up — something the POV character chooses to minimise rather than confront. ESCALATION SEED: this minimised problem starts small here, must reappear with greater pressure at the midpoint, and explodes at the climax.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Inciting Disturbance — the first crack in the ordinary world
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Same familiar environment, a slightly more private or pressured corner of it
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Introduces the central dramatic question of the novel in miniature; the reader senses the protagonist is already making the wrong choice.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Offer or the Order
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: An external force — a person, an institution, a deadline — presents the POV character with a demand or opportunity they cannot ignore. They must make a visible, consequential decision before the scene ends.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: An external force — a person, an institution, a deadline — presents the POV character with a demand or opportunity they cannot ignore. They must make a visible, consequential decision before the scene ends.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Call to Action — protagonist is pulled out of equilibrium
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: A threshold space — doorway, office, street corner — signalling transition
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Locks the protagonist into the plot engine; refusal is no longer a safe option, establishing the book's central conflict.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The First Cost
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Accepting (or refusing) the demand immediately costs the POV character something concrete — a relationship strains, a resource is spent, a door closes. The cost is small enough to seem manageable but large enough to be felt.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: Accepting (or refusing) the demand immediately costs the POV character something concrete — a relationship strains, a resource is spent, a door closes. The cost is small enough to seem manageable but large enough to be felt.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Crossing the Threshold — no clean return to the ordinary world
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: A new or altered environment that reflects the changed situation
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Demonstrates that the world of the novel operates on real consequences; raises the reader's anxiety about what larger costs are coming.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The New Question
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: The chapter closes not on resolution but on a sharp new question: the POV character discovers or realises something that reframes everything just established — a detail noticed too late, a lie half-glimpsed, a threat made visible for the first time. The reader is propelled forward.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: The chapter closes not on resolution but on a sharp new question: the POV character discovers or realises something that reframes everything just established — a detail noticed too late, a lie half-glimpsed, a threat made visible for the first time. The reader is propelled forward.
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: End-of-day or transitional moment — dusk, a closing door, an empty room
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: States the book's central dramatic question explicitly through action or image, not exposition; every subsequent chapter is the answer to what is posed here.
